fabric-api-base.reason: Shipped by Fabricated (vendored from upstream); every Fabric API module builds on it.

fabric-data-generation-api-v1.reason: Mods' runtime code references its classes; its hooks act only when the fabric-api.datagen property is set. Its tag appender mixin adds a removal method Forge's own tag appender already declares, which Mixin refuses without @Overwrite, so it is left out. Its client item definition collector mixin wraps a lookup in a lambda of finalizeAndValidate that Forge's build doesn't have, so that one handler is left out. Pre-flight disabled the module (and every mod referencing it). Lost, in data generation only: removing entries through a Fabric tag appender doesn't work, and a Fabric model provider also writes item definitions for block items of other mods, and of blocks it gave no block state.

fabric-dimensions-v1.reason: Forge loads DataFixerUpper outside the layers Mixin transforms, so upstream's TaggedChoiceMixin and TaggedChoiceTaggedChoiceTypeMixin would never apply, and V2832Mixin, which casts DataFixerUpper's tagged choice type to the interface they add, would fail when the data fixers are built: the three are left out and the rest of the module loads. Nothing is lost: Forge patches the same schema (V2832) to keep a dimension's generator as it is when its type isn't known (DSL.or with DSL.remainder()), so upgrading a world whose dimensions use a chunk generator type no installed mod registers doesn't fail, which is what upstream's mixins are for (read in Forge 61.2.4, 64.1.5, 65.1.5 and 66.1.0).

fabric-entity-events-v1.reason: Forge's LivingEntity asks the bed's state (BlockState.setBedOccupied, getBedDirection) where vanilla sets the occupied property and asks BedBlock, which upstream's occupation and sleeping direction hooks look for, so pre-flight left them out: SET_BED_OCCUPATION_STATE and MODIFY_SLEEPING_DIRECTION never ran, and the red bed upstream's ALLOW_BED hook stands in for an admitted block in startSleeping and stopSleeping reached Forge's setBedOccupied, which set a red bed in the world in the block's place. Fabricated's in-game mod runs both events at Forge's calls and sets the occupied state of the block that is there (SLEEP-1). Forge 61's patch of LivingEntity.hurtServer drops vanilla's copy of the damage before blocking, the second float local upstream's after-damage hook reads, so the hook read the damage a shield blocked instead and ServerLivingEntityEvents.AFTER_DAMAGE reported it as the damage dealt: the in-game mod fires the event at the method's end with the damage applyItemBlocking is asked about, vanilla's copy (DAMAGE-1).

fabric-events-interaction-v0.reason: Forge's destroyBlock no longer calls Block.playerWillDestroy and Block.destroy itself, where upstream's hooks fire PlayerBlockBreakEvents.BEFORE and AFTER: both moved into a private removeBlock Forge added, so pre-flight left the two hooks out and the events never ran when a player broke a block (a mod refusing a break, or acting on one, saw nothing). Fabricated's in-game mod fires them at the same points of Forge's method instead, BEFORE (with CANCELED when refused) once the game's checks pass and AFTER once removeBlock removed the block, before the drops (BREAK-1).

fabric-key-binding-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's API, its key bindings registered on Forge's key mapping event, where Forge mods register theirs. Upstream refuses a key binding once the game's options exist, and Forge 61 creates them before it loads mods, the Fabric client entrypoints among them, so passed through, the module failed every client entrypoint that registers one (KEYMAP-3). Forge loads the keys from the options file again once mods have loaded, which gives each key binding the key the player saved. As upstream, a key binding registered twice is refused, and so is one registered once Forge's event has added them; its category is sorted into the controls screen's order by upstream's mixin; KeyBindingHelper.getBoundKeyOf reads Forge's getKey, where upstream's accessor mixin reads the field.

fabric-loot-api-v3.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's builder and drop mixins as they are, its loading hook replaced by Forge's LootTableLoadEvent (upstream's conflicts with Forge's loot loading).

fabric-particles-v1.reason: Forge 61 replaced the grass check in TerrainParticle's constructor, which upstream's block dust tint hook looks for, with its block extensions' areBreakingParticlesTinted, so pre-flight left the hook out and ParticleRenderEvents.ALLOW_BLOCK_DUST_TINT never ran: Fabricated's in-game mod asks the event where Forge decides the tint instead (PART-2).

fabric-renderer-api-v1.reason: Forge 61's screen effect finds the block the player's view is inside in a method of its own (getOverlayBlock), which returns its position too, and no longer calls vanilla's lookup, where upstream's hook reads the position: pre-flight left the mixin out, and the effect showed a Fabric model's particle sprite without the level. Fabricated's in-game mod gives the level-aware one for the block Forge's lookup found (PART-4). Forge 61 also sets a block's breaking particle's sprite again after upstream's hook gave it (TerrainParticle.updateSprite), from the model with its model data: the in-game mod asks Fabric's level-aware sprite there. A model whose class gives its own sprite for Forge's model data, and that neither is a Fabric model nor holds one, keeps Forge's.

fabric-rendering-fluids-v1.reason: Upstream's MixinExtras expression for the overlay sprite (modifyOverlaySprite) matches nothing in Forge 61's patched LiquidBlockRenderer.tesselate, which Mixin treats as a critical failure when the class loads: every client with the Fabric API jar crashed at the first resource reload (run 40427976979). Why it matches nothing is UNVERIFIED: the definitions it names occur there, which is all pre-flight can check. It is left out with modifyNonOverlayCheck, which reads the flag only modifyOverlaySprite sets. Lost: a Fabric fluid render handler's overlay sprite on the sides of a fluid next to glass or leaves; Forge's own overlay drawing stays.

fabric-rendering-v1.reason: Forge 61 keeps block colour providers in a map by registry holder under the name of vanilla's IdMapper by block id, which upstream's colour provider lookup shadows: Fabricated's in-game mod looks providers up in Forge's map instead of upstream's method (COLOR-1).

fabric-resource-conditions-api-v1.reason: Forge 61 decodes each data pack registry entry through its own conditional decoder (ConditionCodec.wrap), where upstream's hook looks for vanilla's decoding of the entry, so pre-flight left that mixin out and fabric:load_conditions in registry entries were ignored: the in-game mod's FabricResourceConditions has Forge's decoder also give no entry where they fail, with upstream's evaluation. Upstream's hook on JSON data loaders (SimpleJsonResourceReloadListenerMixin) loads, its lambda hook bridged to Forge 61's lambda, which also takes the codec (LAMBDA-8).

fabric-resource-loader-v1.reason: Forge 61 loads the game's options before it loads mods, so upstream's hook at their load (onLoad) ran before the Fabric mods' entrypoints had registered their built-in packs and their resource condition types: it enabled no built-in pack that is enabled by default, forgot the ones it had enabled before, and logged each Fabric mod's pack with conditional overlays as unreadable (CORPUS-104). It is left out, and Fabricated's in-game mod runs upstream's processing (DefaultResourcePackStorage) once the entrypoints have run, before the game selects its packs, as on Fabric (FabricDefaultPacks).

fabric-screen-api-v1.reason: Forge 61's input handlers call a screen's keyPressed, keyReleased, mouseClicked, mouseReleased and mouseDragged through Forge's hooks (ForgeHooksClient.onScreenKeyPressed, onScreenKeyReleased, onScreenMouseDrag, ForgeEventFactoryClient.onScreenMouseClicked, onScreenMouseReleased), and the game renderer draws the screen through Forge's, so upstream's wrappers of the vanilla calls are left out: Fabricated's mixins wrap the same calls inside Forge's hooks (ScreenInputEvents), and its before/after render events fire from Forge's ScreenEvent.Render (ScreenDrawEvents), as on Fabric (SCREEN-1). The rest of the module, scrolling's wrapper included, is upstream's.

fabric-tag-api-v1.reason: Forge's tag files already have a remove list, which its tag loader applies, and upstream's FabricTagFile.remove() reads it: upstream's own list conflicts with Forge's, and its tag loader hooks, which apply that list, are left out with it. Fabricated adds fabric:remove entries to Forge's list instead (the in-game mod's TagFileRemoveMixin).
